[spoiler=Vetrnætr] The first snow had begun to drift across the roofs of Heiðabýr, carried by the sharp breath of the northern winds. It was Vetrnætr, the ancient turning of the year, when Jomsland set aside the last days of harvest and embraced the long dark of winter. Even in the age of steel fleets and satellites, the old customs were not forgotten. This year, the Blót carried unusual weight. Eight nationsthe Bobian Commonwealth, Vespuria, Thyven, Tirakan, Dakshina, Nordiheim, the New Balion Empire, and the Marchesansi Leaguehad accepted the High Kings invitation to witness the sacred rites. Some came out of respect, others out of curiosity, and a few to thaw the relations between the EDU and THEP. By dusk, the crowds filled the area around the temple. Thousands of Jomslanders lined the stone road, holding torches that cast golden light across the carved runestones flanking the path. Musicians beat on drums made from oxhide, their rhythm slow and deep, like a heartbeat beneath the earth itself. Inside the long courtyard of the temple, the horses and other animals chosen for sacrifice stood calmly, painted with blue and red patterns. Their fate was not hidden; it was honored. The Goðar, dressed in heavy cloaks of wolf hide, moved among them, whispering the old prayers. When the High King Jorik III and his entourage arrived, silence fell. He stepped before the great stone altar, carved with scenes of gods and ancestors, and raised the ritual blade. 
Þegar veturinn kemur heiðrum við guðina svo að sálir okkar geti stigið upp til Valhöll. 
As winter arrives, we honor the gods so that our souls may ascend to Valhalla. 
The first sacrifice was a great white stallion bred in the northern fjords. A single, practiced stroke of the ritual blade brought it down. Its blood ran into the blóðskál, the ritual bowl. The Goðar dipped pine branches into it, sprinkling the gathered warriors, nobles, and foreign delegates. Some flinched at the droplets. The Delegates of Thyven muttered prayers under their breath. The Bobians tried to appear composed while their boots stuck to the red-soaked earth. But the Jomslanders accepted each drop like a blessing. The sacrifices continued: two bison, three rams, and a boar whose tusks gleamed like ivory. With each offering, the drumming grew louder, and the spectators felt the old world thunder beneath their feet, ancient and alive. When the rites were complete, the Blót became a feast. Great fires were lit across the temple grounds, and the scent of roasting meat filled the cold night. Cauldrons of mead were rolled out, their lids steaming. Skalds took turns reciting sagas of sea-kings, explorers, and battles long past. Warriors from Jomsland and Nordiheim tested each others strength in friendly wrestling matches, while the envoys of New Balion toasted the High King for the honor of witnessing such a ceremony. As the moon climbed high, snow began to fall. In the glowing firelight, it looked like silver drifting through smoke. The High King stood again, lifting a horn filled with mead.
 Við skulum fagna! 
Let us celebrate! 
Thousands raised their horns in answer. The foreign guests followed uncertainly, but they drank all the same. And so Vetrnætr passed, with the sound of song rising into the frozen sky over Heiðabýr.[/spoiler]

The Coal Barons of the eastern League watched the [i]celebrations[/i] of the pagans. They saw as the stallion was gutted before them, then boars, bison, and rams. The Barons looked on in disgust, as if they were looking at the poor. One Baron coughed up black soot as he watched the blood trickle down into the bowl.

"It's a rather ghastly thing, isn't it, Roberto?" 

"Quite, say, are you alright?"

The inquired looks at the bile coughed on the ground.

"Inspection season, nothing to worry about."

When the feast comes, they dine like pigs, feasting on whatever they can get their hands on. Their previous refined demeanour turned to a joke in the wind as they gorged themselves on meat on drink. A fine evening indeed.
